pull_request.title: Software: profile tracker material recording and guard static cut reuse
pull_request.head: codex/material-recording-profile
pull_request.body:
## Executive summary

The matched 100 events × 100 neutral geantinos took 810.953 s for nODD and 13.535 s for ODD. Native sampling attributes 98.9% of recurring nODD samples to Geant4 material-cut association rebuilding: ACTS calls BeamOn(1) per event, causing a full region traversal per material.

The opt-in immutable-geantino reuse experiment reduced nODD to 101.905 s (7.96× overall; steady median 7.425 → 0.150 s). All 32 scalar/jagged ROOT branches match at zero numeric tolerance for all 10,000 probes in both detectors, and all 14 adverse-state controls pass.

## Change

Adds the node-bound benchmark, task-local ODD build/selection, native timers, hierarchy inventory, exact output checks and reproducible evidence report. Both comparators use the same ACTS/DD4hep/Geant4 binaries and DDG4-first bootstrap. Geometry, passive material, identifiers and the normal recorder remain unchanged.

The guard is an explicit experiment for one immutable world and neutral geantinos. It checks every material/cut association and delegates on invalid state; ordinary energy-cut API configuration disables reuse. It preserves the BeamOn(1) lifecycle. DES-024/025 remain DRAFT; ADR-008 and TASK-SOFT-MATERIAL-PROFILE provide context. No detector or general mutable-Geant4 acceptance is claimed.

The report separates parsing, construction, conversion, voxelization, recurring scans, transport/stepping and ROOT writing, with wall/CPU/RSS and source/binary hashes. Earlier mixed-Xerces failures and bootstrap sensitivity are retained; their precise native mechanism remains unresolved. Independent PhysVal assessment at 25fa2d01ca9b135f070a8549d50dfe3b5af4ced2 found no P1/P2 blocker for this bounded characterization. Its P3 timing-boundary wording correction is included; no detector or general Geant4 approval is granted.

## Token accounting

Recovered **41,308,128 input + 205,567 output = 41,513,695 observed tokens** across **8 completed turns and 267 requests**, including both specialist agents and the two explanation follow-ups.

| Contribution | Input | Output | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main work and explanations | 33,052,857 | 170,249 | 33,223,106 |
| SoftEng specialist | 3,828,921 | 17,317 | 3,846,238 |
| PhysVal specialist | 4,426,350 | 18,001 | 4,444,351 |
| **Total** | **41,308,128** | **205,567** | **41,513,695** |

Cached input **40,301,824** and reasoning output **100,184** are subsets, not additional tokens. These are client observations including cached/repeated context, not a billing estimate. Ten duplicate cumulative snapshots were ignored; each parent/child request stream reconciles independently from zero. Import replay adds no entries. The accounting follow-up was active at capture and is excluded until its final boundary can be recovered.

The [canonical journal](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/6d867fe608679f6d98bc1d152442afb5a30a27f2/logs/codex/SESSION-2026-10-21-material-profile.json) owns all eight observations once; the [usage-only inventory](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/6d867fe608679f6d98bc1d152442afb5a30a27f2/logs/usage/USAGE-2026-10-21-pr91-accounting.json) corroborates counters, closed-turn boundaries and attribution. Local checks pass: 33 logging/recovery/document tests, 10 dashboard tests, JavaScript controls, usage validation/build and project-record validation.

## Dashboard and validation

- [x] Updated project/tracking.json for TASK-SOFT-MATERIAL-PROFILE.
- [x] Completed matched and guarded 100×100 runs; exact full-branch comparisons; 14 native guards; 3 tool, 33 logging/document and 28 project-record controls; session and project validators.
- [x] Preserved DRAFT states, scoped experiment boundaries and exact review/evidence revisions in the paired journal.
- [x] Layout main page/R–Z unaffected: no detector geometry, material or layout changes.

See docs/validation/material-recording-profile/README.md for measured results, commands and limitations.

events.text: I’ll check the repository rules and remote runtime, then run matched ODD and nODD benchmarks and profile the dominant phases. I’ll keep generated data out of Git and prepare a Software PR for any justified fix or reproducible benchmark findings.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The `acts-spack` preflight reports changed setup and lockfile fingerprints, plus no verified DD4hep or Geant4 source trees. I’m using that skill and will verify the installed runtime directly. The existing software worktree has only the prior session’s two untracked journal files; I’ll preserve them.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: PRs 77–80 are marked merged, but I’m checking their actual source paths before choosing the benchmark inputs. The profiling branch is now isolated from current main. I’ll also use the repository’s specialist workflow for an independent comparison assessment.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The ODD “Tracker” compact includes the solenoid, so its name alone does not define a tracker-only comparison. I’ll generate a comparison compact that excludes the solenoid, calorimeters, muons and field block while retaining the beam pipe, tracker and passive supports. Both detectors will run 100 events with 100 neutral geantinos per event.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The first matched nODD run has finished DD4hep construction and reached Geant4. Source inspection points to a possible scaling cost: nODD uses many nested assemblies, which may become a large flat set of Geant4 daughters. I’m checking native call stacks and the converted hierarchy before attributing the slowdown.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The profiler confirms that the slow first event includes Geant4 voxel construction, so its timing cannot be treated as per-track transport cost. The next event took about 15 seconds for 100 probes. The required nODD run is continuing; I’m now separating initialization, navigation, material stepping and output costs.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The steady-state profile found a larger cause: almost all sampled time was spent rebuilding Geant4 material/cut associations at the start of each event. ACTS calls `BeamOn(1)` for every event, triggering scans over the large geometry and its many materials. I’m adding phase timers to measure that work separately from transport.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The nODD run continues at roughly 15 seconds per event. In the steady-state sample, material/cut association rebuilding accounts for about 99% of main-thread samples. The first-event profile separately shows voxel construction. That gives a measured distinction between recurring setup work and transport; the converted hierarchy inventory will test what drives the setup cost.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The runtime inventory confirms the flattening hypothesis: nODD has 649,614 daughters directly in the Geant4 world, versus 5 for ODD. nODD also has 661,997 logical volumes and 1,159 instantiated materials; ODD has 440 and 9. Geant4’s source confirms that each run scans the region volume tree for each material, explaining the severe recurring cost.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: I’m testing a software optimization that leaves the physical model intact: reuse material/cut associations only when every logical volume still has the correct material, region and cut object. It will fall back to Geant4’s normal update when those checks fail. I’ll compare the recorded output with the baseline before including it in the PR.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: An instrumentation check caught a measurement artifact: the timing helper changed which weak inline Geant4 symbols were loaded. I’ve excluded those trials and corrected the helper; its control scan now agrees with the original slow path. The untouched 100-event baseline continues, and the guarded optimization is running against the same 10,000-probe setup.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: The first guarded run completed all 100 events in about 102 seconds. Its first 200 probes match the uncached control exactly in all 32 ROOT branches. events.text: Can you explain how you improved the execution time ?
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text:
Most of the time was spent repeating setup before transporting particles.

ACTS calls Geant4’s `BeamOn(1)` for every event. Each call rebuilds the material/cut associations by scanning the geometry once per material. For nODD, that means roughly **662,000 volumes × 1,159 materials ≈ 767 million volume visits per event**, even though the detector is unchanged.

I added an **opt-in reuse prototype** for this fixed-geometry geantino job. It checks that every volume already has the correct material/cut association, then skips the redundant rebuild. Unsupported or changed states fall back to Geant4’s original update. Event boundaries, geometry, materials and particle transport remain unchanged.

That reduced:

| Measurement | Original | With reuse |
|---|---:|---:|
| Typical event after initialization | 7.43 s | 0.15 s |
| Complete 100 × 100 job | 810.95 s | 101.90 s |

The complete job improves by **about 8×** because parsing, detector construction and first-event voxelization still cost time. All **32 output branches matched exactly numerically across 10,000 probes**.

Separately, loading DDG4 before PyROOT avoided the observed ODD parsing crash and reduced nODD’s original startup-order result from roughly 1,570 to 811 seconds. The precise cause of that load-order timing effect remains unresolved.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: Can this be done at initialize ?
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: I’ll check which Geant4 initialization stage creates these associations and whether they can be reused safely from there.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text:
**Yes—for this fixed detector, building the associations once during initialization is the cleaner approach.**

ACTS already calls `G4RunManager::Initialize()`. However, every subsequent `BeamOn(1)` performs **run initialization**, which unconditionally updates regions and rebuilds material/cut associations. Simply moving the first rebuild into ACTS `initialize()` would leave those repeated rebuilds in place. [Geant4 implementation](https://github.com/Geant4/geant4/blob/v11.4.3/source/run/src/G4RunManagerKernel.cc#L609)

A production implementation would:

1. Build the associations after geometry, materials, regions and cuts are finalized.
2. Reuse them during subsequent events.
3. Invalidate and rebuild them whenever relevant configuration changes—including explicit energy-cut vectors.
4. Preserve event seeds and normal run/event callbacks.

With reliably enforced immutability or complete invalidation tracking, this could also replace the prototype’s conservative **per-event volume check** with a cheap state check.

So initialization is the appropriate home for the one-time work; the performance improvement comes from ensuring later run initialization reuses that work. **The current PR demonstrates guarded reuse; it does not yet implement that initialization-based integration.**

MATPROF-SoftEng-02 completed against `e2a01ae90f376914d53942ef81d64d424d2d13f1`. No edits, simulations, dependency changes or further delegation.

**The load-order effect is measured; its precise native mechanism remains unresolved.** Existing evidence does not justify attributing it specifically to weak Geant4 accessor selection.

Measured evidence:

| Existing run | Completed events when inspected | Steady-event median wall / CPU |
|---|---:|---:|
| `nodd-100` | 100 | 14.9446 / 14.9432 s |
| `nodd-bootstrap-100` | 43; still active | 7.4358 / 7.4357 s |
| `nodd-hidden-control` | 2 | 16.8873 / 16.8684 s |
| `nodd-stable-phases` | 2 | 7.5117 / 7.5113 s |

These come from existing `build/jobs/material-profile/<run>/metrics.json`; the incomplete bootstrap value is provisional.

Both steady samples identify the same dominant call chain:

`BeamOn → RunInitialization → UpdateCoupleTable → CreateCoupleTables → ScanAndSetCouple`

`UpdateCoupleTable` accounts for 6192/6259 main-thread samples before bootstrap and 5816/5881 afterward—approximately 98.9% in both. The bootstrap changes the cost substantially without removing the repeated cut-association scan.

Static symbol/disassembly checks establish:

- `G4LogicalVolume::GetMaterial()` is a **strong external definition** in `libG4geometry`, not a weak definition.
- `libG4processes_core` binds that getter and `SetMaterialCutsCouple()` explicitly to `libG4geometry`; neither appears in its weak-bind table.
- Both sampled processes execute `GetMaterial()` in `libG4geometry`, including `_tlv_get_addr`.
- `ScanAndSetCouple` directly reads region/daughter fields, directly recurses, and calls the external material getter/setter. Its hot daughter accesses are already inlined.
- The retained native-helper binaries inspected contain no public weak Geant4 accessor definitions matching the relevant logical/physical-volume methods. This does not reconstruct an unavailable earlier binary.

The samples match UUIDs for DDCore, DDG4, G4geometry, G4run and G4processes_core. This establishes common binary images, while leaving runtime binding/state/address-layout differences unmeasured.

**Both processes still load two Xerces libraries.** UUIDs `30F031B1-48B2-3379-908B-9AB81CA3BBCD` and `D3A4DD97-84D9-3E03-87E4-2B5366A307EB` occur in both samples, with reversed loading order. Therefore DDG4-first avoids the observed parsing crash in these controls; it does not eliminate duplicate Xerces installations.

Suggested report wording:

> Loading DDG4 before PyROOT avoided the observed ODD parsing failure and approximately halved recurring nODD event CPU time in the existing controls. Both bootstrap orders retained the same principal Geant4/DD4hep binary UUIDs and remained dominated by repeated material-cut association scanning. The exact loader, initialization or memory-layout mechanism behind the timing difference has not been established. Final comparisons use the same DDG4-first bootstrap for both detectors and for instrumented controls.

The journal’s earlier assertion that the shim “changed dynamic symbol selection” and hidden visibility “restores the original accessor symbols” should be qualified accordingly.

Reproducible read-only commands included `nm -m`, `llvm-objdump --macho --bind`, `--weak-bind`, and bounded disassembly at `ScanAndSetCouple` offsets `0x1f6c8–0x1f768` and `GetMaterial` offsets `0x7e4ac–0x7e4e4`.

Profile evidence:

- `nodd-steady.sample.txt`, SHA-256 `68e764bac6dd226462fb6d44370f4df570c2f8c2ac60255a543da7954904f493`
- `nodd-bootstrap-steady.sample.txt`, SHA-256 `ea5366782eb4bb6cf3725fc0b802c32e833c0d4f0f65ae3d5bc859e34c6f34d0`
